title: Measuring Homogeneity in AI-Generated Scientific Literature: Are All AI Research Assistants Pointing Scientists in the Same Direction?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: AI-driven convergence in scientific ideation reduces the diversity of scientific inquiry. Demonstrating this empirically has direct implications for science policy and AI tool design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible with guidance: querying 10+ LLMs with hypothesis generation prompts via API and measuring similarity. The prompt design is creative work suited to CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: 10+ models, 50 prompts, measure similarity and identify universally suggested vs model-specific directions. Clear output format.

novelty.reasoning: The homogenization of creative and scientific output by LLMs is well-documented. Multiple papers show LLMs produce narrower output ranges than humans, and scientific writing is converging toward LLM styles. The hypothesis generation survey explicitly warns about convergent research directions. However, no existing work specifically measures inter-model homogeneity in scientific hypothesis generation across 10+ models simultaneously. The Artificial Hivemind framing applied to research ideation is partially but not fully covered.

evidence.source: Homogenization Effects of LLMs on Human Creative Ideation (C&C 2024)
evidence.finding: Demonstrates that LLMs homogenize human creative ideation, with AI-assisted participants producing more similar outputs than those working independently.

evidence.source: We're Different, We're the Same: Creative Homogeneity Across LLMs (2025)
evidence.finding: Shows LLMs return a narrower range of responses to creative prompts than humans, with lower population-level output variability.

evidence.source: Divergent LLM Adoption and Heterogeneous Convergence Paths in Research Writing (2025)
evidence.finding: Documents GPT-driven homogenization of writing styles in scientific literature, with both junior and senior authors shifting toward GPT-style writing.

evidence.source: Survey on Hypothesis Generation for Scientific Discovery with LLMs (2025)
evidence.finding: Comprehensive survey of LLM-based hypothesis generation, noting that scientists tapping the same LLM risk pursuing only highest-probability research questions, leaving intellectual search space unexplored.
